prompt: Please generate an image. Locked painterly style: hand-painted stylized game art, chunky readable shapes, detail painted not modelled, mid-level detail, softer muted colours with gentle saturation, epic and luminous, never grim. The palette's warm gold and cool teal are painted into the surfaces, but the light is flat, even studio light: no strong key light, no cast shadows, no rim light. Use the attached images only as reference as described: the first attachment is always the style reference for palette and brushwork; later attachments are the approved designs to keep. Game-asset reference sheet for 3D modelling, wide landscape 16:9. Plain light neutral grey background, no scene, no sky, no clouds, no floating rock, no ground plane, a soft contact shadow only. Every piece fully isolated with clear space around it, nothing overlapping, nothing touching the edge, arranged in tidy rows, each with a small neat hand-lettered label underneath. GEAR AND PROPS sheet: Redraw of the attached reference sheet to the current spec: keep the same items and names. Six placeable crafting stations in two tidy rows, each a single clean prop with only the furniture that the station needs, no banners, no hanging herbs or meat, no fire light thrown onto the surroundings: top row "Alchemy Table" (a table with a few chunky glowing flasks and a copper still, the liquid glow a clear separate teal and gold zone), "Cooking Hearth" (a stone hearth with a cauldron on a thick hanging frame and a spit, fire as a clear separate emissive zone), "Shipwright Slipway" (a slipway frame of chunky timbers holding a half-built skiff hull). Bottom row "Sailweaving Enchanting Frame" (a heavy frame stretching a sail, its teal light threads painted onto the sail as a separate glowing zone), "Skill-Book Writing Desk" (a desk with a lectern beside it, apart), "Trainer's Practice Dummy & Target" (a practice dummy and an archery target, apart). Chunky timbers and stone, thick legs and frames, no thin rods or ropes. At true scale to the scale figure: tables and desks about waist height (0.9 m), the skiff hull on its slipway about 6 m long. Each item alone in three-quarter front view, in rows by family or tier, with thick chunky proportions: thick blades, solid rope, chunky grips, no thin parts. A plain neutral 1.8 m human silhouette labelled "1.8 m" stands on the sheet for scale, with everything at true scale to it. Title at the top: "Skills kit: crafting stations 2".
